adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for collective team events, appends co-host destination calendars after the organizer’s (`handleNewBooking.ts`: initialize with organizer/eventType destination, then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` only passes `credential.id` into the provider’s `createEvent` (`calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`). Unlike Google (which now selects the calendar by matching `credentialId`), Office365’s `createEvent` still derives the URL from the first destination calendar only (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; ... /me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`). Therefore, when creating an Office365 event for a co-host destination later in the array (especially in mixed-provider setups), it will post to the main host’s calendar id or fail. This is directly shown by the Office365 code always using index 0 rather than the destination corresponding to the credential being processed.
